titleStmt.title: Observational Evidence from Supernovae for an Accelerating Universe and a Cosmological Constant
titleStmt.author: Adam G. Riess et al. (High-z Supernova Search Team)

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Observational Evidence from Supernovae for an Accelerating Universe and a Cosmological Constant

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: High-redshift SNe Ia are observed to be dimmer than expected in an empty Universe (i.e., Ω M = 0 ) with no cosmological constant.

span.label: acceleration of the cosmic expansion
span.quote: A cosmological explanation for this observation is that a po sitive vacuum energy density accelerates the expansion.

span.label: observational-study
span.quote: We present spectral and photometric observations of 10 type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) in the redshift range 0.16 ≤ z ≤ 0.62.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A PARAMETER THAT CANNOT BE USED BECAUSE IT VARIES IS REPLACED BY VARYING IT DELIBERATELY: limiting magnitudes vary FROM FRAME TO FRAME, NIGHT TO NIGHT, AND FILM TO FILM, SO IT IS DIFFICULT TO USE THE ACTUAL DETECTION LIMITS in the simulation - NEVERTHELESS simulations were run VARYING the limiting magnitude, and THIS DOES NOT CHANGE THE RESULTS SIGNIFICANTLY. An unusable measurement becomes a swept parameter, and the sweep is the answer to its own unusability
span.quote: Limiting magnitudes vary from frame to frame, night to night, and film to film, so it is difficult to use the actual detection limits in our simulation. Nevertheless, we have run simulations varying the limiting magnitude, and this does not change the results significantly.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A MORE REALISTIC PRIOR IS ADOPTED, AND THE WORD `REALISTIC` IS THE JUSTIFICATION: a MORE REALISTIC A PRIORI PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTION for extinction HAS BEEN UTILIZED, taken from another group's calculations. **The same physical quantity, in the same year, is treated the opposite way by perlmutter1999, which describes the realistic option and declines it in favour of a conservative one**
span.quote: A more realistic a priori probability distribution for extinction has been utilized from the calculations of Hatano, Branch, & Deaton (1997).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A CORRECTION'S ASSUMPTION IS STATED AND CONTRADICTED IN THE SAME SENTENCE: such a K-correction ASSUMES that the spectral energy distribution of all SNe Ia OF A GIVEN AGE IS HOMOGENEOUS - YET IT HAS BEEN SHOWN otherwise, with a list of references. The step is used, its premise is named, and the premise is reported false, in one breath
span.quote: Such a K-correction assumes that the spectral energy distribution of all SNe Ia of a given age is homogeneous, yet it has been shown

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A SYSTEMATIC ERROR IS MEASURED WITH SYNTHETIC OBJECTS AND THEN SUBTRACTED, AND THE RESULT IS CALLED UNBIASED: a correction BASED ON THE SYSTEMATIC ERROR DETERMINED FROM THE ARTIFICIAL STARS was applied to the measured magnitude TO YIELD AN UNBIASED ESTIMATE. The word `unbiased` is earned by a procedure on objects that were never there
span.quote: A correction based on the systematic error determined from the artificial stars was applied to the measured SN magnitude to yield an unbiased estimate of the SN magnitude.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE SYNTHETIC OBJECTS ARE MATCHED TO THE REAL ONES ON TWO NAMED PROPERTIES: these ARTIFICIAL STARS HAD THE SAME BRIGHTNESS AND BACKGROUND AS THE MEASURED SNe. What makes the simulation stand in for the measurement is an equality on exactly two attributes, and they are listed
span.quote: These artificial stars had the same brightness and background as the measured SNe

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A CLASSIFICATION IS FIXED BY COMPARISON TO EXEMPLARS WHOSE OWN PROPERTY COMES FROM A DIFFERENT MEASUREMENT: final spectral classification IS OPTIMIZED BY COMPARING the observed spectrum to WELL-OBSERVED SPECTRA of the same class AT THE SAME AGE AS DETERMINED FROM THE LIGHT CURVES. The comparison set is selected using a quantity measured by another instrument entirely
span.quote: Final spectral classification is optimized by comparing the observed spectrum to well-observed spectra of SNe Ia at the same age as determined from the light curves.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: COMPARABILITY BETWEEN TWO EXPERIMENTS IS DEFERRED TO FUTURE WORK, AND THE CONDITION IS NAMED: FUTURE ANALYSIS WHICH SEEKS TO LIMIT SYSTEMATIC UNCERTAINTIES AFFECTING BOTH EXPERIMENTS SHOULD YIELD MEANINGFUL COMPARISONS. The present comparison is therefore not claimed to be meaningful, and what would make it so is stated
span.quote: Future analysis which seeks to limit systematic uncertainties affecting both experiments should yield meaningful comparisons.

span.label: residual noise from sky lines remains in the spectra
span.note: what this limits: the spectral typing and redshifts: RESIDUAL NOISE FROM THE SKY LINES REMAINS
span.quote: residual noise from the sky lines remains

span.label: systematic uncertainties in the Cepheid distance scale affect the age estimate
span.quote: systematic uncertainties in the current Ceph eid distance scale

span.label: A modest amount of grey interstellar extinction cannot be excluded by these data.
span.note: what this limits: the acceleration conclusion, against its main rival: WITH THE OBSERVATIONS PRESENTED HERE, WE CANNOT RULE OUT THIS MODEST AMOUNT OF GREY INTERSTELLAR EXTINCTION
span.quote: With the observations presented here, we ca nnot rule out this modest amount of grey interstellar extinction.

span.label: The high-redshift sample is too small to test whether light-curve-shape relations evolve with look-back time.
span.note: what this limits: any claim that light-curve-shape relations do not evolve: PRESENTLY, OUR SAMPLE IS TOO SMALL TO MAKE SUCH A TEST MEANINGFUL
span.quote: Presently, our sample is to small to make such a test meaningful.

span.label: The KS comparison of low- and high-redshift light-curve decline rates is not statistically significant given the sample size.
span.note: what this limits: the KS comparison of decline rates: A KOLMOGOROV-SMIRNOV TEST SHOWS NO SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCE ... BUT THE SAMPLE IS TOO SMALL TO BE STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT - the null is uninformative
span.quote: A Kolmogorov-Smirnov test shows no significant difference in the distributions of the low and high-redshift samples, but the sample is too smal l to be statistically significant.

span.label: Evolution of the supernova population remains a serious unresolved concern.
span.note: what this limits: the whole cosmological inference: EVOLUTION REMAINS A SERIOUS CONCERN WHICH CAN ONLY BE EASED AND PERHAPS UNDERSTOOD BY FUTURE STUD[ies]
span.quote: Although our current observations revea l no indication of evolution of SNe Ia at z ≈ 0. 5, evolution remains a serious concern which can only be eased a nd perhaps understood by future studies.

span.label: The discrepancy between the two light-curve fitting methods must be carried as a systematic uncertainty.
span.note: what this limits: every cosmological constraint quoted: WE MUST CONSIDER THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE COSMOLOGICAL CONSTRAINTS REACHED FROM THE TWO FITTING METHODS TO BE A SYSTEMATIC UNCERTAINTY - the analysis choice moves the answer, so the spread is carried
span.quote: Until then, we must consider the difference between the cosmological constrain ts reached from the two fitting methods to be a systematic uncertainty.

span.label: The result is limited by systematic rather than statistical errors.
span.note: what this limits: the precision of the headline result: OUR DETECTION OF A COSMOLOGICAL CONSTANT IS NOT LIMITED BY STATISTICAL ERRORS BUT BY SYSTEMATIC ONES
span.quote: Our detection of a cosmological constant is not limited by st atistical errors but by systematic ones.

span.label: Remaining systematic uncertainties require further study.
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 7: FURTHER STUDIES ARE NEEDED TO DETERMINE THE POSSIBLE INFLUENCE OF ANY REMAINING SYSTEMATIC UNCERTAINTIES
span.quote: Further studies are n eeded to determine the possible influence of any remaining systematic uncertainties.

span.label: The headline quantity exists only relative to an assumed model of what causes it.
span.note: what this limits: the deceleration parameter reported here: because it is defined at the current epoch while the supernovae span a wide range of redshift, its value can only be determined within the context of a model for its origin
span.quote: we can only determine the value of q0 within the context of a model for its origin

span.label: The nearby comparison sample was cut to match the observing window available at high redshift.
span.note: what this limits: the comparison between nearby and high-redshift supernovae: the nearby sample was limited to light curves beginning no later than about five days after B maximum, to match the age by which the high-redshift observations ended
span.quote: Because of this restriction, we also limited our consideration of nearby SNe Ia to those with light curves which began no later than ∼ 5 days after B maximum

span.label: The colour correction needs a quantity the survey must itself measure well.
span.note: what this limits: the K-corrections applied to these magnitudes: differences in supernova colour at a fixed phase would alter the appropriate correction, so each supernova's colour must be known precisely
span.quote: Differences in SN Ia color, at a fixed phase, would alter the appropriate K-correction. We need to know the color of each supernova to determine its K-correction precisely

span.label: Bayesian statistical inference and Monte Carlo simulation applied to Type Ia supernova data to infer the expansion history and cosmic acceleration
span.quote: we used a Monte Carlo simulation to understand how SNe Ia in our nearby and distant samples were c hosen

span.label: cosmological constant
span.quote: The goal is to provide an independent set of measurements that uses our own techniques and compares our data at high and low redshifts to constrain the cosmological parameters

span.label: K-correction
span.quote: An appropriate K-correction quantifies the difference between the supernova light which falls into a standard passband (e.g., B) at z = 0 and that which falls into the filters we employ to observe a redshifted SN Ia

span.label: color
span.quote: Differences in SN Ia color, at a fixed phase, would alter the appropriate K-correction

span.label: progenitor age
span.quote: Such observations could indicate an evolution of SNe Ia with progenitor age

span.label: light curve shape
span.quote: These include a new derivation of the relation between light curve shape, luminosity, and color from SNe Ia in the Hubble flow using redshift as the distance indicator

span.label: a more realistic a priori probability distribution for extinction → the extinction prior this paper ADOPTS
span.note: THE SAME ADJECTIVE, THE SAME PHYSICAL QUANTITY, THE SAME YEAR, OPPOSITE DECISIONS - and no type in the vocabulary can express it. This paper ADOPTS the option it calls more realistic. perlmutter1999-omega-lambda describes the same option for the same quantity as “a less conservative but more realistic narrow prior” and DECLINES it, keeping the conservative one. **`contradicts` would be FALSE**: neither team contradicts the other, they weigh the same consideration about the extinction prior and rule differently, and each calls its own reasoning `more realistic`. All eight edge types assert that a relation HOLDS between two concepts; not one can say that two papers apply one word to opposite choices. Recorded here, per record, with each row quoting only its own paper - the cross-paper half is this paraphrase, checkable by opening perlmutter1999-omega-lambda. **This is a NEW use of unhoused_relations: all 67 existing rows describe a relation inside one paper, and this is the first pair that spans two.** Q-632 second case; Q-708.
span.quote: A more realistic a priori probability distribution for extinction has been utilized from the calculations of Hatano, Branch, & Deaton (1997).

span.label: q0, the deceleration parameter - MODEL-RELATIVE BY CONSTRUCTION: it is defined at the present epoch while the data span a wide range of redshift, so the paper states the value can only be determined inside a model of what produces the deceleration
span.quote: we can only determine the value of q0 within the context of a model for its origin

span.label: the K-correction - AS A PASSBAND DIFFERENCE: it quantifies the gap between the supernova light falling into a standard filter at zero redshift and the light falling into the filters actually used on a redshifted object, so it is a correction between instruments and not a property of the supernova
span.quote: An appropriate K-correction quantifies the difference between the supernova light which falls into a standard passband (e.g., B) at z = 0 and that which falls into the filters we employ to observe a redshifted SN Ia

span.label: the nearby sample - TRIMMED TO MATCH THE DISTANT ONE: nearby supernovae were admitted only if their light curves began within about five days of B maximum, because that is the window the high-redshift observations could cover, so the two samples were made comparable by discarding data that existed
span.quote: Because of this restriction, we also limited our consideration of nearby SNe Ia to those with light curves which began no later than ∼ 5 days after B maximum

span.label: contradicts → Perlmutter et al. (1997)
span.quote: These results are inconsistent at the ∼ 2σ confidence level with those of Perlmutter et al. (1997), who found Ω M = 0 . 94 ± 0. 3 (Ω Λ = 0 . 06) for a flat Universe and Ω M = 0 . 88 ± 0. 64 for Ω Λ ≡ 0.

span.label: replicates → High-z Supernova Search Team (Garnavich et al. 1998; Schmidt et al. 1998)
span.quote: The results reported here are consistent with other reporte d observations of high-redshift SNe Ia from the High-z Supernova Search Team (Garnavich et al. 1998 ; Schmidt et al. 1998), and the improved statistics of this larger sample reveal the potential influe nce of a positive cosmological constant.

span.label: builds-on → Garnavich et al. 1998; Schmidt et al. 1998; Riess et al. (1998a)
span.quote: Combined with previous data from our High-Z Supernova Search Team (Garnav ich et al. 1998; Schmidt et al. 1998) and Riess et al. (1998a), this expanded set of 16 high-r edshift supernovae and a set of 34 nearby supernovae are used to place constraints on the fol lowing cosmological parameters: the Hubble constant ( H0), the mass density (Ω M ), the cosmological constant (i.e., the vacuum energy density, Ω Λ ), the deceleration parameter ( q0), and the dynamical age of the Universe ( t0).

span.label: color —causes→ K-correction
span.quote: Differences in SN Ia color, at a fixed phase, would alter the appropriate K-correction. We need to know the color of each supernova to determine its K-correction precisely

span.label: High-redshift Type Ia supernovae are dimmer/farther than a decelerating universe predicts — evidence the cosmic expansion is ACCELERATING (q0<0), implying a positive cosmological constant / vacuum energy (ΩΛ>0).
span.quote: a current acceleration of the expansion (i.e., q0 < 0)

span.quote: The χ 2 statistic of equation (4) is well suited for determining the most likely values for the cosmological parameters H0, Ω M , and Ω Λ as well as the confidence intervals surrounding them

span.quote: Yet the dispersion of indi vidual extinctions for a distribution with a mean of 0.25 mag would be σ AB =0.40 mag, significantly larger than the 0.21 mag dispersion observed in the high-redshift MLCS distances
